title: Sheikh Mansour takeover agreed
summary: Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG), fronted by Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, agrees to buy Manchester City. The deal is announced 1 September 2008 (legal completion followed later that month); the club signs Robinho for a then-British-record fee the same day.

sources.outlet: Man City official site (Sheikh Mansour letter, retrospective)

verify_note: Completion date is sometimes given as 23 Sept 2008 rather than the 1 Sept announcement date — confirm which date to anchor the timeline on before publishing.

title: UEFA FFP settlement: fine and squad cap
summary: Manchester City (along with Paris Saint-Germain) is sanctioned by UEFA for breaching Financial Fair Play rules, agreeing a settlement of up to €60m (€20m forfeited immediately, a further €40m withheld conditional on compliance), a Champions League squad cap of 21 players, and limits on transfer spending and wage growth for two seasons.
club_response: City said it would accept the sanctions and not appeal, while stating a "fundamental disagreement" with UEFA's interpretation of FFP rules as they applied to players purchased before 2010 (as reported by Bleacher Report and Gulf News).

title: Der Spiegel / Football Leaks publishes sponsorship documents
summary: Der Spiegel, drawing on the Football Leaks cache, publishes internal emails it says show Manchester City inflated declared sponsorship income from Etihad and Etisalat, allegedly disguising direct ownership-group investment as sponsorship revenue to satisfy UEFA FFP rules. The documents also contain material relating to payments to former manager Roberto Mancini.
verify_note: Manchester City has consistently and strongly denied wrongdoing relating to these documents; the club's exact contemporaneous November 2018 statement has not yet been located/verified with a specific source — add before publishing.

title: UEFA bans City from the Champions League for two seasons
summary: UEFA's Adjudicatory Chamber finds City committed "serious breaches" of FFP and club licensing rules by overstating sponsorship revenue, and bans the club from UEFA club competitions for the 2020-21 and 2021-22 seasons, plus a €30m fine.
club_response: City said it was "disappointed but not surprised" by the decision and confirmed it would appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (as reported by ITV News and CNBC).

title: CAS overturns UEFA ban, cuts fine to €10m
summary: The Court of Arbitration for Sport lifts City's two-year Champions League ban, ruling that most allegations were "either not established or time-barred", while finding City did fail to cooperate with UEFA's investigation — reducing the fine from €30m to €10m for that narrower finding.

title: Premier League refers 115 charges to independent commission
summary: Following a four-year investigation, the Premier League charges Manchester City with 115 alleged breaches of its financial rules: 54 counts of failing to provide accurate financial information (seasons 2009-10 to 2017-18), 14 counts of failing to disclose full details of player/manager remuneration (including former manager Roberto Mancini's pay), 7 counts of breaching Profitability and Sustainability Rules, 5 counts of breaching UEFA financial regulations, and 35 counts of failing to cooperate with the investigation (December 2018 onward).
club_response: "Manchester City is surprised by the issuing of these alleged breaches of the Premier League Rules, particularly given the extensive engagement and vast amount of detailed materials that the EPL has been provided with. The club welcomes the review of this matter by an independent commission, to impartially consider the comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence that exists in support of its position. As such we look forward to this matter being put to rest once and for all." (Manchester City statement, 6 Feb 2023, as widely reported; re-verify exact wording against the club's original released statement before publishing verbatim.)

title: Guardiola: "We are already being condemned"
summary: At his pre-Aston Villa press conference days after the charges are announced, Guardiola says the club already feels judged in public opinion, while maintaining City's trophies were won fairly on the pitch.
verify_note: Exact press-conference date is an estimate based on typical pre-match press timing, not independently confirmed — check against City's actual Feb 2023 fixture list before publishing this specific a date.

title: Hearing opens in London
summary: A three-person independent commission, appointed by the chair of the Premier League Judicial Panel, begins a hearing at the International Dispute Resolution Centre in London, expected to run around 12 weeks.

title: Guardiola: "Everyone is innocent until guilt is proven"
summary: Ahead of the hearing's opening, Guardiola says an independent panel will decide the case and that he is "looking forward to the decision".
verify_note: Exact press-conference date is an estimate ahead of the Sept 2024 hearing, not independently confirmed — check against City's Sept 2024 fixture list before publishing.

title: Hearing concludes with closing arguments
summary: The hearing concludes; the commission retires to consider its written decision. No timetable is given at this point for the ruling.

title: City wins partial victory in separate APT rules challenge
summary: In a legally separate dispute from the 115-charges case, an arbitration tribunal rules that parts of the Premier League's Associated Party Transactions (APT) rules — which govern sponsorship deals with parties linked to a club's owners — are unlawful, including how shareholder loans were excluded from scope, and that the Premier League's 2023 rejection of two City sponsorship deals (First Abu Dhabi Bank, Etihad Aviation Group) was procedurally unfair.

title: APT rules ruled void in full
summary: A further tribunal judgment finds the unlawful elements of the old APT rules cannot be severed from the rest of the rulebook, rendering the whole prior version unenforceable — a further win for City in the separate APT dispute.
verify_note: Only the month (February 2025) is corroborated, not the exact day — confirm before publishing.

title: City and Premier League settle APT dispute
summary: With a further trial due in October 2025, City and the Premier League reach a settlement over new APT rules, avoiding a second trial.
verify_note: Only the month (September 2025) is corroborated, not the exact day — confirm before publishing.

title: Guardiola announces departure
summary: Manchester City announce Guardiola will step down as manager at the end of the 2025-26 season after ten years in charge, having won 20 major trophies.

title: Guardiola: "I trust them"
summary: On leaving, Guardiola says of the club's owners and leadership: "I trust them. I spoke with them and trust how they behave and how they did" — reported as a personal statement of confidence, not a comment on the substance of the charges.

title: Enzo Maresca appointed as Guardiola's successor
summary: Manchester City appoint former Chelsea head coach Enzo Maresca, who previously worked at City as a youth coach and assistant during the 2018-19 treble season, on a three-year deal.
verify_note: One source pattern suggests an announcement around 22/26 May 2026 instead; 29 June 2026 is used here as two independent outlets' datelines agree on it, but this needs a direct check against mancity.com before publishing.

title: Verdict reported: guilty on 114 of 115 charges
summary: David Ornstein (The Athletic) reports that the independent commission has found Manchester City guilty on 114 of the 115 charges. Sanctions are undecided and the process is ongoing; City are expected to appeal. At the time of the report, City are top of the Premier League under new head coach Enzo Maresca.
club_response: "The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality." — Manchester City statement, 25 Sept 2026, as reported by The Independent and others; the club said its position remains consistent with its earlier stance.

title: Commission's decision published; Premier League statement
summary: The Premier League publishes a redacted Core Decision of the independent commission (about 40 pages, with appendices still to follow) and a statement on it. The commission found City in breach on every charge bar one, covering all financial-rules charges for 2009-10 to 2017-18 and three of four cooperation categories, including a "Disguised Funding Scheme" of "sham" sponsorship arrangements part-funded by owner ADUG that it found overstated income by more than £830m over eight seasons (revenue inflated and costs reduced by more than £900m, per the statement). Sanction will be decided at a separate hearing; City says it is innocent and has appealed.

club_response: City said it was "disappointed and surprised by the opinion of the Premier League Commission" (as reported by RTÉ and others) and has consistently denied wrongdoing. Its 1 October appeal statement is quoted in the entry above.
verify_note: The Premier League and decision-PDF pages could not be opened from the research environment; details come from several outlets plus a law-firm summary (Mishcon de Reya). Per coverage the decision is 40 pages / 160 paragraphs and the appendices were unpublished as of 2 Oct. Verify the quoted £830m / £900m figures and the 'Disguised Funding Scheme' wording against the Core Decision text itself.

title: Manchester City lodge appeal against the commission's decision
summary: City lodge a comprehensive appeal against the commission's opinion at 7pm on 1 October, a day before the deadline. The Premier League says an independent three-member Appeal Board will hear it, with a hearing expected within 12 weeks and a decision due within 30 days of the hearing ending; the hearing stays private until publication of the outcome is permitted. Sanction is still to be decided at a separate hearing.

sources.outlet: Premier League — statement: appeal against decision of independent Commission

club_response: City said the opinion "contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact and is unsafe", that "the club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions", and that it "will therefore be relentless, and where necessary proactive, in any and all appropriate regulatory and legal forums" (wording as quoted by UPI, CBS Sports, TeamTalk and others; the club's statement itself was not opened).
verify_note: Statement pages could not be opened from the research environment; the club's wording is as quoted across several outlets. Confirm the 12-week/30-day rule text against the Premier League handbook. The hearing is private, so outcome timing will only be known when published.

title: Four rivals reportedly lodge notices reserving the right to seek compensation
summary: The Times reports that Arsenal, Liverpool, Manchester United and Tottenham have lodged legal notices reserving the right to seek compensation if City are found to have breached the rules, amid concern they could be out of time under the statute of limitations if they waited for the outcome. Coverage after the September 2026 decision says any formal proceedings are likely to wait until the appeals process is exhausted.
